title: Redwood Console - Tracing, Error Analysis & Request Logs Walkthrough
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing and request logs. Focus on how to find request-level traces, link them to request logs, surface root-cause errors, and set up alerting. Customer (Novus Retail) asks about retention, PII redaction, HIPAA, VPC options, and performance impact on latency. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 + HIPAA docs, benchmark spreadsheet, sample trace export, and schedule a PoC pilot with request-log retention settings.
action_items: Jasmine: Send SOC2 + HIPAA compliance docs and pricing (due 2027-08-12)
Carlos: Export example trace + sample request-log query and raw JSON for Novus - share by 2027-08-11
Ben: Provide example problematic request IDs and sample payloads to reproduce errors (by 2027-08-13)
next_steps: Jasmine to send pricing and compliance pack
Schedule 2-week PoC pilot (SE-led) pending Novus sign-off
Carlos to run quick internal benchmark on trace sampling impact and share results
Laura to review KMS/HSM integration notes and confirm requirements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Novus), Ben Ortiz (Platform Eng), Laura Park (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing and request logs. Showed how to pivot from a failing user request to traces, error analysis, and request logs, set up alerts and filter PII. Discussed retention, VPC/private deployments, and HIPAA compliance; agreed to follow-ups.

[00:00] Jasmine Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jasmine from redwood, and carlos and i will take you through the console tracing and request logs, uh we'll aim to keep it pretty practical, show live examples. aisha, ben, laura, thanks for making time.

[00:18] Aisha Khan: hey thanks jasmine, excited to see how this ties into our existing observability, we use datadog for metrics and new relic for traces today, so curious how redwood fits.

[00:28] Carlos Mendes: great, quick intro — i'm carlos, i'm the se that works on tracing and debugging workflows. first slide — i mean first view — in the console you'll see a requests list, you can filter by model, route, status, and importantly request id. we try to make the hop from an elevated error rate to the root-cause as fast as possible.

[00:46] Ben Ortiz: when you say request id, is that the id we get from the api or is it redwood generated? we need it to match with our internal correlation id.

[00:58] Carlos Mendes: good q. by default redwood surfaces our request_id but you can pass a client_correlation_id header and it will show up. there's a mapping column. so you can search both. sometimes the auto-transcription here says 'client corelation' haha, but that's the gist.

[01:20] Jasmine Lee: we'll demo a failing request — common pattern is a spike in truncated responses, or kv cache miss leading to timeouts — and then show the trace waterfall and request logs. carlos will share the trace view.

[01:40] Carlos Mendes: ok switching to console — (screen share detail omitted in transcript) — at the top is a trace timeline, each span is labeled, you can expand to see kernel selection, batching queuing time, token generation, any quantization fallback. note: sometimes the UI labels the quant path 'quan' in older builds, we fixed that in the last minor but you might still see it in exports.

[02:12] Laura Park: quick security q — how long do traces live? and are payloads redacted for pii? we're a healthcare retailer so HIPAA concerns.

[02:25] Carlos Mendes: retention is configurable by tier; hosted default is 30 days, dedicated/private can be set to the retention you need. for PII we have a redaction pipeline — at ingest we can mask fields via regex or a user-specified schema. also we integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption. for hipaa we have a package we can share — SOC2 + HIPAA attestation, and exportable audit logs.

[03:05] Aisha Khan: and for private deployment we could keep logs on-prem?

[03:11] Jasmine Lee: yes for Private deployments logs can be stored in your VPC or on-prem storage, we provide connectors to S3/GCS or your internal object store — and the control plane runs in your network for audit purposes.

[03:30] Ben Ortiz: any perf impact when we enable full traces or increased sampling? we care about p99 latency.

[03:37] Carlos Mendes: good point. tracing is sampling first-class: default is 0.1% for high-volume endpoints, but you can ramp to 100% for specific routes or by user id, and the Canary mode lets you sample aggressively for a subset. our internal benchmarks show negligible p99 delta at low sampling, but i'll attach a benchmark spreadsheet. we'll run a quick 2-node test for you to validate.

[04:10] Aisha Khan: can you trigger alerts from console when error rate crosses threshold?

[04:15] Carlos Mendes: yep, alerting is integrated — you can create rules on error-rate, latency, or a custom log query. rules can trigger webhooks, slack, or pagerduty. the queries use the same query language as request logs.

[04:36] Jasmine Lee: jumping back to demo, here's a failing request id that Ben shared earlier (he pasted it into chat). notice the waterfall — the model compilation span is long then a batch queue spike — you can click the span to see kernel logs and the request payload.

[04:58] Ben Ortiz: i'm seeing an 'out of memory' style error, but it's labeled 'oomk' — transcription sometimes mangles stuff — what does that mean?

[05:08] Carlos Mendes: 'oomk' is a shorthand in our runtime logs for OOM during kernel exec; in the console we translate it to 'OOM during kernel exec' but in raw request logs you might see the runtime shorthand. the key is you can see the exact stack and the surrounding requests in the batch which often reveals if a large context pushed memory above threshold.

[05:43] Laura Park: are those raw logs accessible? we need to ingest them into our security logging pipeline.

[05:49] Carlos Mendes: yes — you can stream request logs to your SIEM or export them as ndjson. note: we can filter or mask payloads before streaming if you need pii redaction.

[06:10] Jasmine Lee: quick aside — customers often ask about linking traces to db calls or internal spans from their app; we support opentelemetry trace id correlation so you can stitch together the full request across systems.

[06:28] Aisha Khan: perfect — we already have opentelemetry tracing; that'll make onboarding smoother.

[06:35] Carlos Mendes: demo continues — using the console's error analysis view, you can group by exception message, model version, region, or canary flag. here's an example where the error rate jumps after a model update; you can roll back or route traffic to the previous model version via the rollout UI.

[07:05] Ben Ortiz: do rollbacks preserve in-flight requests? we're concerned about partial failures during rollouts.

[07:12] Carlos Mendes: rollouts are gradual and you can set automatic fallback policies; in the event of severe errors the system can immediately switch traffic to the safe variant. in dedicated deployments you also get control over drain time.

[07:32] Jasmine Lee: we should call out integration w/ your CI/CD — you can wire the rollout triggers to your release pipeline so the console becomes the control plane for model releases.

[07:46] Laura Park: one more security — where are audit logs stored and how long? we need 12 months for our compliance.

[07:53] Carlos Mendes: audit logs for admin actions are stored in the control plane and we can push them to your own log store; retention is configurable and for private deployments we can meet 12 months or more. we'll include this in the docs pack.

[08:10] Jasmine Lee: switching to request logs view — you can run a live query, filter by status 4xx/5xx, model, route, or custom header. here's an example query that looks for 'timeout' and sorts by response time.

[08:32] Ben Ortiz: what query language is that? is it lucene-like?

[08:36] Carlos Mendes: it's a SQL-ish log query language, similar to kusto, with convenience functions for token counts and latency buckets. we'll send examples. sometimes folks say it looks like datadog queries, but it's its own thing.

[09:00] Aisha Khan: do you keep the full request payload for logs? our lawyers want to know what qualifies as 'full' — e.g., prompt + user metadata + attachments.

[09:10] Carlos Mendes: by default yes we log prompt and metadata, but we recommend enabling PII redaction for sensitive fields or using client-side tokenization. for attachments we can store references only. these are configurable per-route.

[09:28] Laura Park: KMS integration — can we use an HSM-backed key from our cloud KMS?

[09:33] Carlos Mendes: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS + CloudHSM, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. envelope encryption is supported and access to plaintext logs can be restricted via RBAC.

[09:48] Jasmine Lee: demo shows an error analysis drilldown — group by model version, then click into a sample trace — you can re-run a request with a modified prompt in a sandbox to validate fixes. this sandboxed re-run doesn't affect production traffic.

[10:12] Ben Ortiz: nice, re-run would help us reproduce. can we replay a sequence of requests for a failing session?

[10:18] Carlos Mendes: yes, you can export a session as ndjson or replay it via our replay API to a dedicated test pool. useful for debugging stateful issues or cache-related failures.

[10:35] Aisha Khan: what's the difference between request logs and raw engine logs?

[10:40] Carlos Mendes: request logs are structured records at the API layer — headers, latency, status, token counts, and pointer to trace id plus a small runtime summary. raw engine logs are lower-level and can be exported for deeper kernel-level debugging — those are typically enabled for PoC or under support engagement because of volume.

[11:05] Jasmine Lee: (note — slight background phone noise) i'll pause here for any specifics you want us to demo; ben you mentioned a sample request id earlier?

[11:16] Ben Ortiz: yes i pasted it — thanks — i'm also wondering about integration with our incident page, we need direct links from incidents to the console so oncall can jump straight to the trace.

[11:28] Carlos Mendes: we provide a deep-link format, you can include it in your incident document and it will open the trace and highlight the span. deep-links can include ephemeral tokens or be generated via the api with limited lifetime.

[11:45] Laura Park: does the console mask secrets in logs? we sometimes leak auth headers by accident.

[11:51] Carlos Mendes: we have a secrets masking list; by default common auth headers are masked. you can also add custom header names or regex to the redaction list.

[12:05] Aisha Khan: ok real world constraint: our legal team needs proof for HIPAA and that logs aren't accessible to 3rd parties. how do we prove that?

[12:15] Jasmine Lee: we'll share our HIPAA attestation and SOC2 report. for hosted we have contractual terms and you can request a BAA; for private you control the runtime and storage. i'll include the legal checklist in the follow-up email.

[12:34] Ben Ortiz: returning to sampling — if we set sampling to 100% for a particular user group, will that spike our logging cost significantly?

[12:44] Carlos Mendes: yes cost scales with retention + sample volume. Redwood Optimize can recommend an efficient sampling policy based on your traffic and token distributions so you can capture enough signal without exploding cost.

[13:05] Jasmine Lee: quick demo of the trace search — we'll search for errors during today's timeframe, group by error type — here you can pin a trace, annotate it, and add it to an incident timeline. team members with RBAC permission can redact sections before export.

[13:28] Aisha Khan: if we want to onboard a single route to 100% tracing for a week, what support do you offer?

[13:35] Carlos Mendes: SE-led onboarding; we also provide a checklist — config for sampling, PII redaction policies, ingestion endpoints for your SIEM, and a performance runbook. for high-touch pilots we allocate a support engineer.

[13:58] Ben Ortiz: any gotchas with quantized models? we saw a regression on a quantized variant a while back.

[14:06] Carlos Mendes: quantization can change kernel selection and memory use; in the console trace you'll see a quantization span. we recommend running release canaries with synthetic prompts to detect regressions; the console can run those synthetic evals and tie them to error analysis.

[14:30] Jasmine Lee: switching to request-log query examples, here's a query that finds \"incomplete output\" and groups by model version. i'll paste it in chat after.

[14:44] Ben Ortiz: please do. also can we export logs to our S3 with encryption?

[14:49] Carlos Mendes: yes, export to your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS key. we'll include sample terraform for the connector.

[15:05] Aisha Khan: timeline — we're looking to pick a vendor by end of september and start a pilot in october. realistic?

[15:13] Jasmine Lee: yes that timeline works. pilot typically 2-4 weeks. we'll send a tailored pilot plan.

[15:24] Laura Park: what about egress restrictions — can the console only talk to certain IPs?

[15:29] Carlos Mendes: for private we support strict egress control and the control plane can be in your VPC. hosted supports IP allowlists and private peering.

[15:46] Ben Ortiz: any references of other retail customers with HIPAA-ish constraints?

[15:52] Jasmine Lee: we have a healthcare-retail reference; i'll connect you with their PM.

[15:59] Carlos Mendes: looping back to debugging flows — here's how you'd triage: 1) identify spike via metrics 2) drill to error analysis 3) pick a representative trace 4) follow spans and inspect batch neighbors 5) if needed, export raw engine logs and replay. this gives a repeatable runbook for oncall.

[16:20] Aisha Khan: sounds good, could we see a quick replay example?

[16:24] Carlos Mendes: quick demo — i export a session and push it to a test pool; the replay shows identical latency distribution. note: replay strips identifiable user tokens by default but you can configure that.

[16:45] Ben Ortiz: one more thing — we run some synchronous user flows and p99 matters a lot; do you have out-of-the-box dashboards for p50/p95/p99?

[16:53] Carlos Mendes: yes built-in dashboards and per-route dashboards. you can also build composite dashboards combining model metrics and your custom metrics.

[17:08] Jasmine Lee: (checks chat) ok a couple of questions in chat: can we limit who can export raw logs? answer: yes via RBAC and audit logs. next: can we anonymize before export? yes via the redaction pipeline.

[17:26] Laura Park: will we be able to use our SSO?

[17:29] Jasmine Lee: we support SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we'll include SSO setup steps in the onboarding doc.

[17:40] Aisha Khan: good. any potential blockers you foresee for our setup?

[17:45] Carlos Mendes: a few things to confirm: whether you want hosted vs dedicated vs private, expected trace volume and retention, and any legal constraints for BAA. once we have that we'll size and propose pricing.

[18:00] Ben Ortiz: pricing question — is logging charged separately from tokens?

[18:05] Jasmine Lee: yes token usage is separate; logs and retention are a different billing line — we'll provide a sample cost breakdown. optimize can give recommendations to reduce log cost by dynamic sampling and prefix caching.

[18:26] Aisha Khan: curious how you correlate failures to model versions across regions — we run multi-region traffic.

[18:33] Carlos Mendes: trace metadata includes region, model version, and commit id. the console can group errors by region and perform histograms; you can also set routing policies per region in the control plane.

[18:52] Jasmine Lee: we're about halfway through — do you want us to pivot to a deeper kernel-level debug or keep the higher-level UX flow?

[18:59] Aisha Khan: high-level is good for now; we might schedule an SE deep dive next week.

[19:08] Carlos Mendes: noted — we'll prepare a kernel-level session showing raw engine logs, kernel selection and memory timelines.

[19:18] Ben Ortiz: can you show a sample alert rule and the webhook payload?

[19:22] Carlos Mendes: sure — alert rule triggers include context like trace id, model version, and a link to the console; webhook payload is JSON with a summary and a direct deep link. i'll paste an example.

[19:40] Jasmine Lee: demo finishing — quick recap: we showed trace UI, error analysis, request logs queries, re-run/replay, PII redaction, KMS + RBAC, and alerting.

[19:52] Aisha Khan: that's helpful. next steps from our side: legal will review the HIPAA pack, platform team will share example request ids for reproduction, and security will review KMS integration.

[20:05] Jasmine Lee: perfect — our next steps are to send the docs pack, pricing and pilot plan, and schedule the SE deep dive kernel session.

[20:18] Ben Ortiz: when can we get the benchmark spreadsheet?

[20:22] Carlos Mendes: i'll run an internal quick test today and share the numbers tomorrow, and attach the spreadsheet.

[20:31] Laura Park: can we have the PoC start doc to send to legal?

[20:35] Jasmine Lee: yes i'll include a short PoC starter and the legal checklist.

[20:44] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone.

[20:47] Jasmine Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up by e-mail with the artifacts.

[20:52] Meeting end (approx)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "oomk" shorthand), product names sometimes slightly off, and speaker punctuation is rough.
